cards.text: This psalm kicks the door open with "Hallelujah!" and calls people to praise the name of the LORD. No warmup, no stretching. Me? I need three hits of the snooze button before I'm that excited about ANYTHING.

cards.question: The psalm calls one group to give praise first. Who is it?

answers.text: The servants who stand in His house
The kings who rule the nations
The shepherds who watch the flocks

cards.text: Then comes Hallelujah number two. And this time the psalm tells you why.

cards.question: The psalm says to praise the LORD because He is good.

cards.text: It says to sing praises to His name, "for it is lovely." And now the reasons start stacking up like cookies on a cooling rack.

cards.question: Next reason: the LORD has chosen Jacob as His own. What does the psalm call Israel?

cards.text: Then the psalm writer speaks for himself: "For I know that the LORD is great;" Not "I think." Not "I'm pretty sure." I KNOW.

cards.question: The psalm writer says our Lord is ___ all gods.

cards.text: How great? The LORD does all that pleases Him in the heavens and on the earth. Friend, I can't even get a tray of cookies to do what pleases ME.

cards.question: The psalm says the deep seas are the one place the LORD can't do what pleases Him.

cards.text: Now look up. He causes the clouds to rise from the ends of the earth, and He makes the lightning with the rain. He runs the LIGHTNING, and I can't get my oven to heat both sides of the tray the same.

cards.question: The psalm says the LORD brings forth the wind from His storehouses.
Then the psalm leaves the sky and goes to Egypt. The LORD struck down the ___ of Egypt, of both man and beast.

cards.text: Then the psalm talks right TO Egypt: He sent signs and wonders into your midst, against Pharaoh, Egypt's king, and all his servants. Imagine being one of those servants. You didn't pick this fight. You just clocked in.
And He keeps going. He struck down many nations and mighty kings: Sihon, king of the Amorites, Og, king of Bashan, and all the kings of Canaan.

cards.question: With Sihon, Og and the kings of Canaan struck down, what does the psalm say the LORD did with their land?

answers.text: Gave it to Israel as an inheritance

cards.text: Then the psalm stops talking about the LORD and talks straight to Him: "Your name, O LORD, endures forever," FOREVER, friend. My name got carved into a handle, and I still ended up in a junk drawer.

cards.question: The psalm says the LORD's renown lasts for just one generation.

cards.text: Then comes a promise. The LORD will vindicate His people.

cards.question: The LORD will vindicate His people and will have ___ on His servants.

cards.text: Then the psalm takes a hard turn and looks at the idols of the nations. Silver and gold. Shiny, I'll give them that.

cards.question: Who does the psalm say made the idols of the nations?

cards.text: Now the psalm gives these idols a checkup. They have mouths but cannot speak, and eyes but cannot see. That's not a god, friend. That's a VERY expensive paperweight.

cards.question: The psalm says the idols have ears that can hear.

cards.text: No hearing, and no breath in their mouths either. All that silver and gold, and it can't even fog up a window.

cards.question: The psalm says something happens to those who make idols and to all who trust in them. What is it?

cards.text: Now the psalm wraps up with a roll call, starting with "O house of Israel, bless the LORD;" It's like a group chat where EVERYBODY gets tagged.

cards.question: After the house of Israel, which priestly family does the psalm call to bless the LORD?
After the house of Levi, the psalm also calls everyone who fears the LORD to bless Him.

cards.text: Then one last blessing. Blessed be the LORD from Zion, He who dwells in Jerusalem.

cards.question: This psalm opened with "Hallelujah!" How does it end?

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "This psalm kicks the door open...", "No warmup, no stretching.", "Me?" and "I need three hits of the snooze button...". The opening card allows three at most.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The joke "You didn't pick this fight. You just clocked in." casts Pharaoh's servants as innocent bystanders in God's judgment. That makes God's judgment the target of the humor. It also states something about the servants that the text does not support: Exodus 10:1 says the LORD hardened the hearts of Pharaoh's servants.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: Jacob appears here for the first time with no simple introduction. A baker could take him for Jacob the man and not the people of Israel.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question keeps "of both man and beast". That phrase rules out the wrong answers "rulers" and "armies", because "rulers of beasts" makes no sense. The baker can drop those two answers from the wording alone.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Handed it back to Egypt" is not believable. Egypt never held the land of Sihon, Og or Canaan in this passage, so "back" makes no sense.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
